statement: First recognized human SHAV infection reported in France; patient treated for serious illness died in early October.
source_title: ECDC: Severely ill patient in France becomes first ever human infected with Shamonda virus
limitations: Acquisition and contribution to death remain under investigation.

statement: French authorities describe cerebral complications as very probably associated with SHAV in a severely immunocompromised patient.
source_title: Inserm: Virus Shamonda : une première détection chez l’être humain
limitations: No detailed peer-reviewed case report or causal demonstration in this announcement.

statement: A Culicoides bite in eastern France is the authorities’ working hypothesis.
source_title: Inserm: Virus Shamonda : une première détection chez l’être humain
limitations: The route is unconfirmed; no established human transmission parameters follow.

statement: No human-case sequence accession or deposition link was identified in the inspected ECDC and Inserm announcements.
limitations: This is not proof of global absence; independent NCBI queries and missing-host counts are recorded in the data manifest.

statement: SHAV detection was associated with fever, diarrhoea, lethargy and milk-yield reductions in affected European herds.
source_title: Wernike et al. Emergence of Shamonda Orthobunyavirus, Central Europe, 2026. Emerging Infectious Diseases. DOI:10.3201/eid3212.261496
limitations: Early release; observational association does not establish universal severity or human phenotype.

statement: Clinical pathology and evidence of intrauterine exposure supported an association with congenital abnormalities in Japanese calves.
source_title: Hirashima et al. Congenital Malformations of Calves Infected with Shamonda Virus, Southern Japan. Emerging Infectious Diseases. DOI:10.3201/eid2306.161946
limitations: No quantitative risk estimate or demonstrated European-variant phenotype follows.

statement: Partial SHAV-related sequences were recovered from an aborted South African goat fetus collected in 2021.
source_title: van der Walt et al. Identification and Molecular Characterization of Shamonda Virus in an Aborted Goat Fetus in South Africa. Pathogens. DOI:10.3390/pathogens12091100
limitations: Partial genome; isolation unsuccessful. Publication year differs from collection year.

statement: Culicoides-mediated spread is the accepted model; vertical transmission has been reported; WOAH identifies no evidence of direct animal-to-animal transmission.
source_title: WOAH: Shamonda virus questions and answers
limitations: Vector species and European epidemiology remain incompletely characterized.

statement: S encodes nucleocapsid protein N and nonstructural protein NSs.
source_title: Suda et al. Complete genome sequences of Sathuperi and Shamonda viruses isolated in Japan. Journal of Veterinary Medical Science. DOI:10.1292/jvms.23-0275
limitations: Gene identity does not establish variant-specific immune evasion or human pathogenicity.

statement: M encodes the glycoprotein precursor containing Gn, Gc and NSm.
source_title: Suda et al. Complete genome sequences of Sathuperi and Shamonda viruses isolated in Japan. Journal of Veterinary Medical Science. DOI:10.1292/jvms.23-0275
limitations: Divergence alone cannot establish altered tropism, antigenicity or transmissibility.

source_title: Suda et al. Complete genome sequences of Sathuperi and Shamonda viruses isolated in Japan. Journal of Veterinary Medical Science. DOI:10.1292/jvms.23-0275
limitations: Sequence conservation does not measure replication or clinical phenotype.

statement: EU1 denotes the initial southern-Germany/France/Switzerland clade; EU2 denotes a second clade initially identified in north-western Germany and related to Japanese SHAV across all segments.
source_title: Wernike et al. Two incursions, two viruses: emergence of a second novel Shamonda virus clade, Germany, 2026. Eurosurveillance. DOI:10.2807/1560-7917.ES.2026.31.39.2600756
limitations: Provisional nomenclature. Do not label individual sequences from country alone.

statement: EU2 data are linked to PRJEB125115; earlier German EU1 data to PRJEB123174. Individual accession labels require verified record links.
source_title: Wernike et al. Two incursions, two viruses. Eurosurveillance. DOI:10.2807/1560-7917.ES.2026.31.39.2600756
limitations: Sample, isolate and segment assignments come from the accession records, not accession order.

statement: The initial French accessions are PZ797891–PZ797893; subsequent genomes are OZ516531–OZ516536. Initial S is partial despite broader abstract wording.
source_title: Kelleci et al. Detection of a novel Shamonda Orthobunyavirus in dairy cattle, France, June 2026. Eurosurveillance. DOI:10.2807/1560-7917.ES.2026.31.33.2600689
limitations: The August statement about no human infection evidence is superseded by the October announcement.

statement: French nucleotide phylogenies suggested possible reassortment; German amino-acid trees reported no evidence of interlineage reassortant origin.
source_title: Kelleci et al. Detection of a novel Shamonda Orthobunyavirus. Eurosurveillance. DOI:10.2807/1560-7917.ES.2026.31.33.2600689
limitations: Compare with Wernike EID row. Neither establishes donor, direction, timing or phenotypic consequence.

statement: WOAH reports no commercially available SHAV vaccine and little apparent cross-protection from prior Schmallenberg immunity.
source_title: WOAH: Shamonda virus questions and answers
limitations: No licensed human treatment claim verified here; EU1/EU2 cross-protection remains unconfirmed.
